purpose: Joint central-versus-surrounding spectral context across all seven existing cohort epochs, both fixed frames, all five discovery references and every historical covering native order; no classifier or origin assignment.

fixed_geometry.core_basis: Union of five historical +/-0.25 A cores: catalog extrema 3869.7450 and 3869.7575 A, centered at their midpoint. No fitted width.
fixed_geometry.grid: 601 points -3 to +3 A in 0.01 A steps

order_inventory_decision.coverage_basis: Exact original individual event topocentric center and native FITS-header endpoint pair; distinct from common groupcenter and fixed plotting anchor.

normalization_and_support: Retain signed flux. Fixed pooled native-sample flank median, 1.5<=|offset|<=3 A, requires >=20 finite native samples separately on both sides and positive pooled median. Missing/nonpositive references stay raw-only. Preserve native gaps/outside coverage; no clipping, absolute normalization, extrapolation or smaller-window fallback. No fitted background.
prospective_header_coverage_caveat: The three selected order2 exposures cover their event center but their upper wavelength edges preclude the full positive normalization flank. They must retain missing-right-flank outcomes where confirmed by fixed sampling. This differs from C001 order3 missing-left-flank context. Order3 header coverage is broad enough; no flux-quality outcome is assumed.
frame_interpretation: The first catalog discovery fixes the topocentric plotting center for every epoch and every reference. Each exposure has a different expected topocentric location for a barycentric-coherent feature. At this BERV span the feature can leave the fixed core; a later-reference topocentric core then describes the fixed anchor neighborhood, not that exposure's own feature center. Report both frames/all references and surrounding pattern without recentering or treating one whole-core correlation as a physical-origin test.
